about: Stages and timing for the test-and-learn playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: find
stages.do: Measure what each rule does to the query, add the findings, and ask the user which one to test.

stages.name: test
stages.do: Set up an A/B test of today's rule against a fixed variant (Pattern 2), and start it after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the find stage found nothing worth testing.

stages.name: read-out
stages.do: Read the test's result. Don't stop early on a good-looking day.

skip_when.reason: the test stage was skipped, so no test is running.

stages.name: close
stages.do: End the test keeping the winner (or today's rule), check every rule, then archive it, each step after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the read-out was skipped: there is no result to act on.

stages.name: confirm
stages.do: Check the shipped change holds at full traffic, with the change and its live date from the hand-off file.

skip_when.reason: nothing changed for shoppers, so there is nothing to confirm.
the close was skipped: nothing was rolled out.

notes.min_test_days: Days after the test stage finishes (the test started) before the read-out stage is due. discovery-experiment-setup recommends at least 14 days in whole weeks; use the end date agreed at setup when it's later.
notes.measure_after_days: Days after the close stage finishes (the winner went to full traffic) before the confirm stage is due. change-impact-tracker needs about 14 days of data after a change for a verdict other than too early to tell.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then.
notes.finding_verdicts: rule_impact.py verdicts that become findings. Rules that help or are neutral are left out unless the findings command gets --all.
notes.next_skill: The skill that acts on a finding, by verdict. A rule that hurts or hides sellers is tested before it's changed, so the next skill is discovery-experiment-setup.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when an earlier stage had one of these outcomes, or with skipped: true when it was skipped). A stage may also name the product it needs; status suggests skipping it when the run doesn't have that product. max_chosen (default 1) is how many findings a run may act on at once.
